analysis: What changed vs the 7:00 AM brief: the early-session drift turned into a deeper slide. Nvidia broke below Monday's $155.01 low, trading $152.12 (-2.57%) by 10:57 AM ET with a day low of $150.33 — the premarket bounce is fully reversed and then some, and the stock is -14.86% over five sessions. Two fresh Huang headlines landed in the last hour: the Dec 1 House-committee testimony is confirmed (Reuters, committee statement), while the NY Post's report that the board is not considering reinstating him — and has hired Wachtell Lipton, with DOJ probes into Megaspeed and Supermicro — is single-source, though CBS reported a similar board stance on Nov 16. The macro tape split: October retail sales were resilient in the core (+0.6% vs 0.4% expected, control group +0.6% vs 0.3%), which keeps December-hike pricing near 95-97%, while the NAHB index fell to 25, its lowest since April 2012, and Home Depot's outlook trimmed the top of its EPS range — housing remains the soft spot. Megacaps are mostly lower (MSFT -1.1%, GOOGL -0.6%, META -0.6%) with AAPL flat and TSLA/AMZN slightly green; UBS's fresh Buy initiations on AMZN ($340) and META ($815) did not lift the tape. Breadth stays weak: Monday's NYSE decliners outnumbered advancers 3.45-to-1 and volume ran below the 20-day average. Signal vs noise: everything still funnels into Nvidia after the close; the testimony date and board stance are real overhangs, the retail-sales strength is a genuine data point for the rate path, and the opticals bounce from the 7:00 AM brief has no fresh follow-through yet. Community: no qualifying thread this hour — the freshest HN Nvidia stories are 1-5 points with 0-1 comments, and the Reddit search returned nothing.

headlines.headline: Fourth straight down day taking shape: S&P 500 -0.40% to 7,386.69, Nasdaq -0.34% to 24,425.89, Dow -0.70% to 51,246.98 at 10:24 AM ET; the Nasdaq is in correction territory, more than 10% below its Oct 6 closing high. VIX ~22.9.
headlines.why_it_matters: The slide is deepening rather than stabilizing into the late morning — sellers are still in control with Nvidia's print hours away.

headlines.headline: Nvidia slid to $152.12 (-2.57% vs Monday's $156.14 close) by 10:57 AM ET, with a day low of $150.33 — below Monday's $155.01 low. The stock is -14.86% over five sessions and -28.96% over one month. Earnings land after the close (~4:20 PM ET, call 5:00 PM ET).
headlines.why_it_matters: Breaking Monday's low after the premarket bounce failed shows there is no dip-buying ahead of the print — the market is de-risking into the numbers, not positioning for them.

headlines.headline: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to transcribed interviews with several House committees on Dec 1, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said Tuesday (Reuters); Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter appears Dec 2. The interviews cover whether Nvidia's China sales endangered national security and will be transcribed but not televised.
headlines.why_it_matters: A dated, official congressional appearance keeps the China-export and governance overhang on the calendar into December — it does not resolve with tonight's earnings.

headlines.headline: Nvidia's board is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, despite calls from Elon Musk and other tech leaders, sources told the NY Post; the board has hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate Huang, and Nvidia still faces DOJ probes into its Megaspeed and Supermicro dealings plus a shareholder class action. Polymarket puts a Huang return by year-end at 8%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile. If true, it closes the 'Huang comeback' trade that had been supporting the stock, though CBS reported a similar board stance on Nov 16.

headlines.headline: October retail sales rose 0.2% MoM, in line with expectations; core sales +0.6% vs 0.4% expected and the GDP-relevant control group +0.6% vs 0.3% expected, with sales +6.8% YoY. Auto sales fell, offsetting gains elsewhere; in real terms the headline read was roughly flat after 0.4% October CPI.
headlines.why_it_matters: The stronger core/control-group detail keeps December-hike pricing near 95-97% — resilient consumers give the Fed room to tighten, which is the headwind over growth multiples.

headlines.headline: NAHB/Wells Fargo builder confidence fell 4 points to 25 in November, the lowest since April 2012 (expected 29); buyer traffic fell to 16 and 46% of builders are cutting prices, the highest share since the Covid period.
headlines.why_it_matters: Housing is the clearest weak spot in the economy — it pairs with Home Depot trimming the top of its EPS range and keeps homebuilders and housing-exposed names under pressure.

headlines.headline: Home Depot shares fell ~1.7-1.9% after Q3: sales $43.4B beat the $42.8B expected and comp sales rose 2.2%, but adjusted EPS of $3.86 was roughly in line with estimates, and fiscal 2026 guidance lifted sales growth to ~4.5% (top of range) while cutting adjusted EPS growth to ~2%, dropping the top of the prior flat-to-4% range. CFO Richard McPhail becomes CEO Nov 23.
headlines.why_it_matters: The market is trading the profit outlook, not the sales beat — sales growing faster than profit, plus a CEO transition, is why the Dow's drag is still dragging.

headlines.headline: Megacaps mostly lower late morning: MSFT -1.1% to $512.49, GOOGL -0.6% to $281.95, META -0.6% to $622.65, AAPL flat at $352.82, AMZN +0.1% to $258.04, TSLA +0.4% to $381.18. UBS initiated coverage on AMZN (Buy, $340 target) and META (Buy, $815 target); Barclays reiterated TSLA Overweight.
headlines.why_it_matters: Fresh Buy initiations on AMZN and META did not lift the tape — analyst support is not offsetting the Nvidia-led AI selloff or the rate-hike headwind this morning.

headlines.headline: October industrial production fell 0.4% vs +0.1% expected (Fed G.17, 9:15 AM ET); capacity utilization 76.4% vs 76.8% expected. Manufacturing rose 0.3% while utilities fell 4.3%, giving back September's weather-driven jump; total IP was still +2.1% YoY.
headlines.why_it_matters: Carried from the 7:00 AM brief: a headline miss driven by utilities payback, not factory demand, so it did not move December-hike pricing.

headlines.headline: Disney held its early recovery after the fiscal Q4 beat (adjusted EPS $1.77 vs $1.67 expected, revenue $25.9B, +16%); streaming operating profit doubled to $824M, content investment rises 9% in the new fiscal year and the dividend was raised by a third. The quarter included a 53rd week adding ~$1.6B of revenue.
headlines.why_it_matters: Carried from the 7:00 AM brief: one of the few early-session recoveries — streaming strength and the dividend hike are getting a second look, though the 53rd-week caveat still flatters the beat.
